reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: The conceptual lineage traces back to von Neumann's minimax theorem (1928) and Shannon's information theory (1948), which established that optimal play in zero-sum games requires maximizing information gain. This was later formalized in dynamic programming by Bellman (1957) and applied to sports through optimal stopping theory. The idea that football resembles chess crystallized in the 1960s with the advent of systematic film analysis and playbook structuring.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: Opposing agents (coaches, players) are modeled as bounded rational expected utility maximizers operating under asymmetric information. They must infer the opponent's hidden state (formation, play type) while concealing their own. The primitive "brain over speed" captures the agent's ability to perform online Bayesian updates faster than opponents can react, creating a persistent informational rent.
